messages:
lucas: Quick microbench on sparrow-lite (9B-ish). Compared fp16, int8, and int6 on 1k mixed slices (short chat, structured extract, long summary). Dropping a rapid GTN/product handoff.

mei: Paste the headline scorecard pls.

lucas: Scorecard (1k):
```
metric           | fp16  | int8  | int6  | note
QA F1            | 0.902 | 0.895 | 0.873 | int8 ~0.8% drop vs fp16
Exact Match (EM) | 0.847 | 0.840 | 0.816 | int6 worst on extraction
ROUGE-L          | 0.452 | 0.445 | 0.424 | long summaries hurt more
Latency p50 ms   | 98    | 110   | 122   | kv-cache mismatch increases p95
Cost / 1k tok    | $0.48 | $0.34 | $0.24 | int8 ~29% down, int6 ~50% down
```
Short notes: priming (2-system tokens) helps int8 stability on short QAs. int6 shows larger regressions on multi-bullet extraction and numeric unit normalization.

dan: Routing recommendation for GTN? one-sentence for product.

lucas: Suggest tiered default: exploratory -> int6, standard product -> int8, critical extraction/longform -> fp16. Add simple fallback: shadow 1% int6/int8 to fp16 and auto-fallback to fp16 if EM delta > 2% over 20m.

mei: Any runtime guardrails to include?

lucas: Minimal set:
- Shadow 1% traffic to fp16, rolling EM & QA F1 deltas, page if delta > 2% sustained 20m.
- Hourly adversarial probe (100 examples) targeted at extraction + numeric tests.
- If int8/int6 p95 latency > fp16 p95 * 1.3 and error rate increases, throttle to fp16.

bench-bot: canary scheduled: bench/canary-420999 -> 1k requests over 1h; full report to #eng-ml/bench-reports.

dan: Product blurb I'll use: "~30% token cost reduction with int8 (vs fp16), ~50% with int6; expected average accuracy drop: int8 ~0.7-1.0%, int6 ~2-4% (workload dependent). Recommend tiered routing + 1% shadowing and hourly adversarial checks"

lucas: I'll upload per-slice breakdown when the canary finishes.
